data.description:
## Description

**What**: Add the new dso:verification-remediation-planner agent (model opus) with the deterministic ordered decision tree from SC3: (1) zero AC evidence for any criterion -> replan_story; (2) all criteria have partial evidence and gap is implementation-only -> new_tasks_in_story; (3) criterion requires new user-facing behavior not in current story -> new_story_in_epic; (4) criteria span multiple epics -> replan_epic. The planner reads the verifier's full output (criteria_results, evidence_searched, remediation_tasks_created) directly via Read. Emits the {scope, target_id, decomposer_context, escalation_upstream, confidence} envelope. Tree is evaluated in order with short-circuit semantics — the first matching rule wins; ties between rules of equal precedence yield confidence LOW.

**Why**: SC3 — sprint's verifier-fail remediation currently drafts inline from the verifier's `remediation_tasks_created` hint. The planner is the canonical handler that supersedes inline drafting, reading verifier output directly and emitting a structured directive that downstream decomposers consume.

**Scope**:
- IN: Agent definition `plugins/dso/agents/verification-remediation-planner.md` with model opus, decision-tree rules, output schema, tiebreaker rules
- IN: Synthetic-verifier-output fixtures exercising each of the 4 decision-tree branches + an overlap case for tie-breaker validation
- OUT: Sprint caller-side wiring at Phase F Step 18, Phase G Step 2, d039-ac65 (delivered by SC3 sprint wiring story)
- OUT: Touchpoint embeddings consuming the planner's escalation_upstream (delivered by SC4 touchpoint-embedding story)

## Done Definitions

- The new dso:verification-remediation-planner agent exists with model: opus and a documented schema for {scope, target_id, decomposer_context, escalation_upstream, confidence}
  ← Satisfies: sc-3
- Planner evaluates the 4-branch decision tree in the SC's documented order (1 zero-AC → replan_story; 2 all-partial+impl-only → new_tasks_in_story; 3 new-user-behavior → new_story_in_epic; 4 multi-epic → replan_epic) with short-circuit semantics — the first matching rule wins. Synthetic-verifier-output fixtures exercise each of the four decision-tree branches and the planner returns the correct scope value per the ordered rules
  ← Satisfies: sc-3
- When two rules of equal precedence tie after documented tiebreakers, the planner emits confidence == LOW; in all single-rule-match cases it emits confidence != LOW. A synthetic fixture includes an overlap case (verifier output that would match rule 2 AND rule 3 if rules ran in parallel) and asserts the planner returns the rule-2 outcome with non-LOW confidence (short-circuit on first match)
  ← Satisfies: sc-3
- The planner's emitted decomposer_context references verifier output by absolute path and includes the target_id and escalation_upstream consistent with the chosen scope
  ← Satisfies: sc-3

## Considerations

- [Determinism] Decision-tree rules must be evaluated in order with explicit tiebreakers — document tiebreakers in the agent definition so behavior is reproducible.
- [Contract] escalation_upstream is consumed by the SC4 touchpoint-embedding story; settle on the upstream enum values jointly with the shared-protocol story (brainstorm / preplanning / planner_supplied).

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a sprint orchestrator, I want a new dso:verification-remediation-planner (opus) that classifies verifier failures via a deterministic ordered decision tree and emits a structured remediation directive
